properties.note: Post authorship is recorded in postHistory (UserId identifies the poster, PostId the post), so a user's posts are the postHistory rows where UserId equals users.Id rather than the posts.OwnerUserId column.
A vote is tied to the post it was cast on, so any user-to-vote attribution must pass through postHistory.PostId.
Post value/quality is measured by posts.FavoriteCount, so the most valuable post is the one with the maximum favorite count, not the most viewed.
In this database the stored age category 'adult' covers ages 19 through 65 inclusive, so adult users are selected with a BETWEEN range rather than a lower-bound-only test like Age >= 18.
CreationDate is stored as a text datetime like '2012-02-22 19:46:04.0', so compare calendar days with date(CreationDate) = 'YYYY-MM-DD' rather than matching against another table's date column.

A post belongs to the user identified by posts.OwnerUserId, so ownership/author questions join users to posts on that column rather than through postHistory, which records other users' activity on a post.
The number of views a post received is stored in posts.ViewCount, and posts with no recorded views hold NULL in that column.
When a post's id is requested together with the post title, the id is the owner user's id from users.Id, linked to the post through posts.OwnerUserId.
The commenter is identified by comments.UserId, which references users.Id, so questions about comment authors link comments to users on that pair.
A person referred to by name in the question is identified by the users.DisplayName text value.
Datetime columns are stored as text like '2011-01-03 11:13:42.0', so a day-level filter matches with a date prefix.
Popularity is measured by the view count, and comparing users' popularity requires summing ViewCount over all of that user's posts rather than looking at a single post.
The badge award date is a DATETIME text value in 'YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS.0' form, so the calendar year is extracted with STRFTIME('%Y', badges.Date).
The posts a user owns are identified by posts.OwnerUserId; postHistory rows are edit-history records and do not represent a user's posts.
Badge names are stored as fixed case-sensitive labels, so the commentator badge is exactly 'Commentator'.
View popularity is measured by the posts.ViewCount integer column, and the most-viewed item is the one with the largest value.
The post's score value is the integer column posts.Score, summed directly.
Votes carry no user column, so votes attributed to a person are the votes on the posts recorded in that person's postHistory entries.
A tag is identified by its plain name in tags.TagName (no angle brackets or delimiters), so an equality filter on the raw name is the correct condition.
The user who owns a post is identified by posts.OwnerUserId matching users.Id, and that user's display name is users.DisplayName.
The number of views for a user is stored in users.Views; posts.ViewCount is a different measure (views on a post) and should not be substituted.
The user behind a post history entry is postHistory.UserId, which matches users.Id for the user's name.
Post score is posts.Score, and the highest-scoring post is obtained by ordering by that column descending.
A user's posts are found through postHistory authorship (postHistory.UserId = users.Id, postHistory.PostId = posts.Id), not through posts.OwnerUserId.
Tag names are stored lowercase without angle brackets in tags.TagName, so the R language tag is the exact value 'r' (not '<r>' in posts.Tags).
A person's age in whole years is stored in users.Age (teenager 13-18, adult 19-65, elder above 65), and it may be NULL when unknown.
Votes carry no user column, so votes attributed to a person are the votes on the posts recorded in that person's postHistory entries.
When comparing two counts as a ratio, cast the numerator to REAL so the division is decimal instead of truncated integer division.
A user's posts are linked through postHistory (UserId to PostId), so posts and users must be joined via postHistory rather than through posts.OwnerUserId alone.
The stored age category 'teenager' spans 13 to 18 inclusive.
comments has no timestamp column, so recency of a comment is expressed by ordering on the CreationDate of the user associated with the post.
A user's posts are found through postHistory authorship (postHistory.UserId = users.Id, postHistory.PostId = posts.Id), not through posts.OwnerUserId.
comments.Score is a 0-100 rating where a score above 60 defines a positive comment (below 60 is negative).
badges.Date is a DATETIME stored as text like '2011-07-20 00:02:13.0', so the calendar year of an award is extracted with STRFTIME('%Y', badges.Date) rather than by string slicing.
Votes carry no user column, so votes attributed to a person are the votes on the posts recorded in that person's postHistory entries.
In the same 0-100 rating scale, a score below 60 defines a negative comment.
A user's posts are linked through postHistory (UserId to PostId), so posts and users must be joined via postHistory rather than through posts.OwnerUserId alone.

"Only one post history" for a user means the user has exactly one distinct history type (postHistory.PostHistoryTypeId) across the qualifying posts, so count distinct types grouped by postHistory.UserId rather than counting history rows per post.

The number of favorites a post received is stored per post in posts.FavoriteCount (may be NULL), so a 'favorites of at least N' condition is posts.FavoriteCount >= N rather than a sum over post history.
The stored age category 'elder' is any age strictly greater than 65.
Tags used by a person means the posts that person authored via postHistory, returning the posts.Tags values.
The rating given to a comment is stored in comments.Score as an integer from 0 to 100, where 0 is the lowest score.
users.Id is the integer primary key identifying a user account and is non-null, so it is the column to count for user counts.
When ranking users by popularity, group results per user (users.DisplayName) and order by the summed view count, returning the user's DisplayName instead of a post title.
Post tags are stored directly as text in posts.Tags, not in a separate tag-name table.
Post creation timestamps are recorded in postHistory.CreationDate, so counting posts created on a given day means counting postHistory rows whose creation date matches that day.
A post is identified by its Title text, and comments attach to it via comments.PostId = posts.Id.
A vote is tied to the post it was cast on, so any user-to-vote attribution must pass through postHistory.PostId.

Each post history entry is its own row in postHistory keyed by postHistory.Id and linked to a post via postHistory.PostId, so describing the history of a titled post returns one row per history entry rather than a COUNT aggregate.

Badge names are stored in exact Title Case with multi-word values (e.g. 'Supporter', 'Popular Question'), so equality must match the stored casing exactly since SQLite text comparison is case-sensitive.
Posts related to a given post are the ones whose postLinks row has PostId pointing to it, so join posts.Id = postLinks.PostId rather than including the RelatedPostId side.
Tags attach to posts through tags.ExcerptPostId = postHistory.PostId, so tag usage is counted by joining tags to the user's postHistory rows.
Votes carry no user column, so votes attributed to a person are the votes on the posts recorded in that person's postHistory entries.
The user attached to a vote (including its bounty) is the voter, resolved as users.DisplayName via votes.UserId = users.Id, not the post author.
"Highest" among views is expressed by comparing users.Views to the maximum users.Views, which returns every user tied at that maximum instead of a single arbitrary row.
Each comment is one row in comments, so counting comments.Id counts the comment rows attached to the qualifying posts.
The user who owns a post is identified by posts.OwnerUserId matching users.Id, and that user's display name is users.DisplayName.
The post's last edit timestamp is stored in posts.LastEditDate as a DATETIME value.
The number of comments on a post is stored in posts.CommentCount, so restricting to posts with a given comment count filters on that column rather than by counting comment rows.
When a question gives a single calendar date for a post, filter on posts.LasActivityDate (the last activity date), not the creation date.
A post is well-finished/closed when posts.ClosedDate is populated (non-null); a null or empty ClosedDate means it is not finished.

Each post history entry is its own row in postHistory keyed by postHistory.Id and linked to a post via postHistory.PostId, so describing the history of a titled post returns one row per history entry rather than a COUNT aggregate.
In this database the post's title text is stored in postHistory.Text, so identifying a post by its title means filtering postHistory.Text.
Each row in badges is one awarded badge, identified by badges.Id, so badge counts can be taken directly from badges without joining users.

Post authorship is recorded in postHistory (UserId identifies the poster, PostId the post), so a user's posts are the postHistory rows where UserId equals users.Id rather than the posts.OwnerUserId column.
The commenter is identified by comments.UserId, which references users.Id, so questions about comment authors link comments to users on that pair.
User location is stored as free text in users.Location (values such as 'United Kingdom', 'London, United Kingdom'), so a country filter is an equality check on users.Location.
Post-tag associations live in the tags table (one row per post's tag), so a question about posts carrying a given tag should be answered from tags, not from the posts table's delimited Tags string.
A user's posts are identified by posts.OwnerUserId; postHistory.UserId records who interacted with a post and does not identify the owner.
When comparing two counts as a ratio, cast the numerator to REAL so the division is decimal instead of truncated integer division.
The voter is recorded in votes.UserId, and votes must be counted from the votes table rather than inferred from postHistory entries.
The title of a post is stored in posts.Title (many rows have a NULL title).
The comments table stores only PostId and Text, so there is no comment-author user id; the user linked to a comment is reached through the post's owner (posts.OwnerUserId = users.Id).
The database defines teenager as age 13 through 18 inclusive; age 19 is classified as adult, so teenage predicates must exclude 19.

A post belongs to the user identified by posts.OwnerUserId, so ownership/author questions join users to posts on that column rather than through postHistory, which records other users' activity on a post.
A user's posts are linked through postHistory (UserId to PostId), so posts and users must be joined via postHistory rather than through posts.OwnerUserId alone.
A bounty placed on a post is recorded in votes.BountyAmount, where the voter is votes.UserId and the target post is votes.PostId.
Tags attach to posts through tags.ExcerptPostId = postHistory.PostId, so tag usage is counted by joining tags to the user's postHistory rows.
When a question asks which users, return the human-readable name from users.DisplayName (often alongside users.Id), not the numeric id alone.
A user's posts are found through postHistory authorship (postHistory.UserId = users.Id, postHistory.PostId = posts.Id), not through posts.OwnerUserId.
Post popularity is stored in posts.ViewCount and a minimum-views request compares posts.ViewCount directly (the column may be NULL for some posts).
Each post is a single row keyed by the integer posts.Id, so queries about which posts qualify should project posts.Id rather than an aggregate over the whole table.
The user associated with the most recent revision of a post is posts.LastEditorUserId, and their name comes from users.DisplayName via users.Id.
The creator/owner of a post is recorded in posts.OwnerUserId, while posts.Id links to post history rows.
A user's posts are found through postHistory authorship (postHistory.UserId = users.Id, postHistory.PostId = posts.Id), not through posts.OwnerUserId.

A post whose title mentions a topic is matched with a LIKE '%term%' filter on posts.Title, and the matched posts.Title should be included in the output when the question identifies the post by its title.
A user's posts are linked through postHistory (UserId to PostId), so posts and users must be joined via postHistory rather than through posts.OwnerUserId alone.
Comments carry no score of their own; the score discussed for comments is the score of the post the comment belongs to, reached by joining comments.PostId to posts.Id.
users.LastAccessDate is a DATETIME stored as 'YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS.0', so compare dates with date(users.LastAccessDate) to avoid counting rows from the boundary day.
A user's posts are identified by posts.OwnerUserId; postHistory.UserId records who interacted with a post and does not identify the owner.
